articles.title: Iran Walked Away From the Table. India's Oil Clock Just Started Ticking Faster.
articles.excerpt: Tehran suspended ceasefire talks after Israel struck Tyre, the US hit Qeshm island, and global oil inventories fell toward their lowest levels since 2003.
articles.image_caption: US Navy vessels patrol near the Strait of Hormuz
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World Is Running Out of Oil Reserves. India Cannot Afford to Wait.
articles.excerpt: The EIA warned that OECD oil inventories are headed to their lowest levels since 2003. India, which imports 85% of its crude, faces an existential squeeze.
articles.image_caption: Industrial oil storage tanks amid the global energy supply crisis
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Bill Wants to Kill the H-1B Green Card Pipeline. Every Indian Worker in America Should Read It.
articles.excerpt: Rep. Chip Roy's American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act would end dual intent, eliminate OPT, and cut the visa to two years. If it passes, the rules of the game change entirely.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Chip Roy of Texas, sponsor of the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US House Just Cleared a $70 Billion Bill to Fund ICE Through the End of Trump's Term.
articles.excerpt: The legislation passed its procedural vote 213-211. No new oversight. No reforms. And a fully funded enforcement machine that will define the next three years for every immigrant in America.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol in Washington, DC, where the House voted on the immigration enforcement bill
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Downed a US Apache Over the Strait of Hormuz. India's Fragile Oil Lifeline Just Got More Fragile.
articles.excerpt: A Shahed drone reportedly struck the helicopter. Both pilots survived, but the ceasefire Trump promised is unravelling — and India's $90-a-barrel nightmare is back on the table.
articles.image_caption: A US Army AH-64 Apache attack helicopter in flight
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Indian Workers Died on a Dubai Highway. A Truck Stopped. A Bus Didn't.
articles.excerpt: A minibus carrying workers slammed into a stalled truck on Emirates Road. Seven are dead, nine injured. The Indian Consulate is at the hospital.
articles.image_caption: A multilane highway in Dubai, similar to Emirates Road where the fatal crash occurred
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Remittances Hit $43.5 Billion in One Quarter. The Gulf Crisis Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: India posted a surprise current account surplus in Q4 FY26 — and the money flowing home from frightened workers in West Asia is what made it possible.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Heads to France and Slovakia This Week. It Is India's First PM Visit to Bratislava Ever.
articles.excerpt: The six-day European tour covers the G7 summit in Evian, a startup showcase in Nice, and the first Indian prime ministerial visit to Slovakia since the country's independence in 1993.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Will Have Half a Million AI Agents Within Three Years. Hiring Will Shrink.
articles.excerpt: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran told shareholders that AI workers will match TCS's human headcount — and that the days of mass IT hiring are over.
articles.image_caption: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran at a corporate event
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US and Iran Say a Deal Is Days Away. India Needs It More Than Anyone at the Table.
articles.excerpt: A ceasefire framework that reopens the Strait of Hormuz would begin to reverse the worst energy supply crisis India has faced in years — but the gap between 'largely negotiated' and 'signed' has been wide before.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil transits
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eight Workers Burned Alive at Vizag Steel Plant. A Crane Carrying Molten Iron Collapsed.
articles.excerpt: The deadliest industrial accident at India's flagship steel plant in years has reignited questions about ageing equipment, safety lapses, and the cost of privatisation delays
articles.image_caption: Entrance to the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Delhi Hotel Was Licensed for Six Rooms. It Was Running Twenty-Five. Twenty-Two People Are Dead.
articles.excerpt: The Malviya Nagar fire has killed 22 people, including 13 foreign nationals, and exposed a fire safety crisis in the capital's unregulated hospitality sector
articles.image_caption: South Delhi's Malviya Nagar area, where a licensed-for-six hotel was running 25 rooms when fire killed 22 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Congress Tells Modi: You Pocketed the Cheap Oil. Now Swallow the Expensive Kind.
articles.excerpt: A 76-page opposition report says India has slipped to the world's sixth-largest economy, the rupee has hit a record low, and the government is passing the Iran war's costs to consumers
articles.image_caption: A Bharat Petroleum fuel station in India
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Cut the Cost of Bringing Dollars Home. NRIs, This One Is for You.
articles.excerpt: A concessional forex swap at half the market rate, leverage on NRI deposits, and a $50–70 billion inflow target — India's central bank is pulling every lever to defend the rupee.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sent a Delegation to Russia Last Month. It Came Back Talking About Coal Mines.
articles.excerpt: SAIL and NMDC are exploring acquisitions of coking coal assets in Russia and boosting nickel imports — a quiet but significant pivot in India's raw materials strategy.
articles.image_caption: Molten metal pouring in a steel mill blast furnace
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Hormuz Blockade Has a Hole. Nearly 3 Million Barrels a Day Are Slipping Through.
articles.excerpt: Ghost tankers with transponders off, Qatari LNG carriers paying tolls, and clandestine dark transits — the supposedly sealed Strait of Hormuz is leaking oil. For India, it may be the difference between a crisis and a catastrophe.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker sailing on the open sea
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Indian Tech Exhaled.
articles.excerpt: Judge Leo Sorokin called it an unauthorized tax. Only 85 companies had paid it. The White House says it will appeal — but for now, the most punitive visa fee in US history is dead.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. federal courthouse — where a Massachusetts judge struck down the Trump administration's 00,000 H-1B fee (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Chief Just Arrived in India. An Indian Astronaut Is Headed to the ISS.
articles.excerpt: Bill Nelson's India visit cements the most ambitious phase of US-India space collaboration yet — an ISS mission, a Goddard Award for Chandrayaan-3, and a commercial space station offer on the table.
articles.image_caption: NASA Administrator Bill Nelson, who arrived in India this week for meetings with ISRO leadership
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Expect a Trade Deal Within Weeks. The Tariff Threat Still Looms.
articles.excerpt: A two-way agreement is on the table, but India wants a written guarantee: no future tariffs after the deal is signed. Washington has not yet agreed.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who is leading trade negotiations with Washington
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Moved the EB-2 India Green Card Line Backward by 10 Months. Thousands Are Stuck Again.
articles.excerpt: The June 2026 visa bulletin pushed the EB-2 India final action date to September 2013 — erasing nearly a year of progress for Indian professionals waiting for permanent residency.
articles.image_caption: A US Citizenship and Immigration Services facility processes visa applications
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Biscuit Packet Is Smaller. Your Petrol Bill Is Higher. India Inc Is Passing the War to You.
articles.excerpt: From Hindustan Unilever to Maruti Suzuki, Indian companies are hiking prices and shrinking product sizes as the Iran war drives up oil, freight, and raw material costs across the board.
articles.image_caption: An Indian consumer goods store stocked with household products and groceries
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Goldilocks Economy Is Over. The Iran War Broke It.
articles.excerpt: GDP growth projected to slow to 6.7% in FY27 as oil at $97, a weak rupee, and fertiliser shortages create overlapping supply shocks that the RBI cannot simply cut its way out of.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, the nerve centre of India's monetary policy response
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A US Fighter Jet Hit an Oil Tanker in the Gulf of Oman. All 24 Sailors on Board Were Indian.
articles.excerpt: The Palau-flagged MT Marivex tried to run the American blockade four times before an F/A-18 from the USS Abraham Lincoln disabled it. Omani authorities rescued the entire Indian crew.
articles.image_caption: An F/A-18 Super Hornet launches from the USS Abraham Lincoln, the carrier whose jet disabled the MT Marivex
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Indian Air Force Will Fly NEET Papers to 18 Military Hubs. The Paper Setters Are Already in Lockdown.
articles.excerpt: After the May exam was cancelled over a leaked paper that matched 120 questions, India is treating the June 21 re-exam like a military operation. For 22.79 lakh students, a second chance hinges on a chain of custody that now runs through the armed forces.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force transport aircraft — IAF planes will deliver NEET question papers to 18 military hubs nationwide
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Opposition Just Met in Delhi. Kharge Told Them the Economy Is Broken and Modi's Government Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: The INDIA bloc's latest show of unity comes as inflation crosses the RBI's target, fuel prices climb for the fourth time in three weeks, and the opposition tries to build on a rare Lok Sabha victory.
articles.image_caption: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addresses party leaders at the INDIA bloc meeting in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Monsoon Arrived Three Days Late. For an Economy Already Burning Through Oil Reserves, That Delay Matters.
articles.excerpt: The southwest monsoon hit Kerala on June 4, later than the June 1 normal. As it crawls toward Mumbai and Delhi, India's farmers, power grid managers, and inflation watchers are all counting the same thing: days.
articles.image_caption: Monsoon clouds over the Indian coast — the southwest monsoon arrived in Kerala on June 4, three days late
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran and Israel Say They Have Stopped Shooting. India Says It Is Watching.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi expressed utmost concern as missiles flew. The Strait of Hormuz is still closed. Oil is still near $97.
articles.image_caption: Map of the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint through which a fifth of global oil passed before the war
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Filed for Its IPO. SpaceX Goes Public Thursday. Anthropic Filed Last Week.
articles.excerpt: Three trillion-dollar AI companies are racing to public markets in the same quarter. Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas says he is watching closely.
articles.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, which filed for a U.S. IPO targeting a $1 trillion valuation
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook Used His Last WWDC to Bet Everything on a New Siri. Apple Has Been Late Before.
articles.excerpt: Siri AI, built on Google Gemini, can read your screen, recall old conversations, and run third-party agents. India's 100 million iPhone users are watching.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook at his final WWDC keynote as Apple CEO before handing over to John Ternus in September
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ZEE Grabbed the FIFA World Cup Rights Ten Days Before Kickoff. It Paid 40% Less Than FIFA Wanted.
articles.excerpt: After JioStar balked at the price, ZEE swooped in at $60 million, launched a new sports network, and bet its future on Indian football fandom.
articles.image_caption: FIFA World Cup 2026 decorations ahead of the tournament starting June 11
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Gets the Owner's Box. Mamdani Bought Standing Room. Both Are at the Knicks Game Tonight.
articles.excerpt: NYC's Indian-origin mayor — son of filmmaker Mira Nair, former rapper, Cuomo slayer — is hosting a rival watch party for 5,000 while the president sits in the suite.
articles.image_caption: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the city's first Asian American and Muslim mayor
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Broadcom Missed One Number by $1.2 Billion. It Triggered the Worst Chip Selloff Since 2020.
articles.excerpt: The AI trade's tolerance for imperfection hit zero. Wipro crashed 8.4%, Korea tripped a circuit breaker, and $923 billion in semiconductor value vanished in two days.
articles.image_caption: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan, whose AI chip guidance miss triggered a global semiconductor rout
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil India Hits Gas Twice in the Andaman Sea. India's Most Promising Frontier Basin Just Got Real.
articles.excerpt: Two successful wells out of three in less than nine months. With the Strait of Hormuz half-shut and oil at $97, the timing could not be more pointed.
articles.image_caption: An offshore platform in India's eastern offshore waters during a naval exercise

sources.label: Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri post on X

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched a Fuel That Costs ₹20 Less Per Litre. Your Car Cannot Use It.
articles.excerpt: E85, an 85 percent ethanol blend, went live at 48 stations on World Environment Day. But only flex-fuel vehicles — a tiny fraction of India's fleet — can fill up.
articles.image_caption: Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who launched India's E85 flex-fuel programme
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Centre Just Cut Ujjwala Subsidised Cylinders from Nine to Four. Ten Crore Households Will Feel It.
articles.excerpt: The government says the average Ujjwala family uses only four refills a year. Critics say that average exists because families cannot afford more.
articles.image_caption: A domestic LPG cooking gas cylinder of the kind distributed under the Ujjwala scheme
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CBSE Dumps the Vendor Behind Its Exam Scandal. IIT Has Built a Replacement.
articles.excerpt: Coempt EduTeck's portal had expired security certificates, multiple data access vulnerabilities, and was hit by a 3.8-million-packet cyberattack. The new IIT-audited system is now live.
articles.image_caption: Students at a board examination centre in Kolkata
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensodyne's Parent Is Building a ₹2,000 Crore Factory in India. It Will Be the Company's Largest Plant Anywhere.
articles.excerpt: Haleon, maker of Sensodyne, Centrum, and Crocin, will build its first Indian manufacturing site in Madhya Pradesh — a bet on India becoming the hub for its entire Asia supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Sensodyne toothpaste, one of Haleon's flagship oral care brands driving its India expansion
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Posted a Surprise $7.1 Billion Surplus Last Quarter. The Diaspora Sent the Money.
articles.excerpt: Remittances from Indians working abroad surged 28% to $43.5 billion in a single quarter — the largest jump in years — as Gulf-based workers transferred funds home amid the West Asia crisis.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Crossed the RBI's Red Line. Fuel and Vegetables Did the Damage.
articles.excerpt: Consumer prices likely rose 4% in May — breaching the central bank's target for the first time in 15 months — as four fuel price hikes and a punishing heatwave pushed transport and food costs sharply higher.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — inflation has crossed the central bank's 6% upper tolerance band
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Found a New Legal Route to Tariff India. This Time, It May Stick.
articles.excerpt: After two court defeats killed Trump's emergency tariffs, USTR Jamieson Greer is using a forced labor investigation to impose a 12.5% surcharge on Indian goods — with no expiration date and no cap.
articles.image_caption: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who authored the 98-page Section 301 report targeting 60 economies
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Just Agreed to Triple Their Trade to $50 Billion. The Largest-Ever Indian Delegation Flew to Ottawa to Seal It.
articles.excerpt: Piyush Goyal led 112 Indian companies to Canada for CEPA negotiations, a trade forum launch, and a handshake with Mark Carney. For 1.8 million Indian-Canadians, the thaw could not come sooner.
articles.image_caption: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who led India's largest-ever business delegation to Canada
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Crossed 150 GW of Solar Power. Then It Had to Switch Off a Sixth of It.
articles.excerpt: The country added a record 44.6 GW in a single year and became the world's third-largest solar market. But the grid cannot absorb what the panels produce, and the paradox is getting worse.
articles.image_caption: The Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan, part of India's rapidly expanding solar infrastructure
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SEBI Says 99.8% of Rajesh Exports' Subsidiary Revenue Was Fabricated. The Number Is ₹15.15 Lakh Crore.
articles.excerpt: India's market regulator has barred the gold exporter and its billionaire chairman from the securities market, alleging the largest revenue inflation in Indian corporate history — routed through a Swiss refinery that actually earned a fraction of what the books claimed.
articles.image_caption: SEBI Bhavan, the headquarters of the Securities and Exchange Board of India in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Raised Fuel Prices Four Times in Three Weeks. The Oil Minister Says They Will Fall.
articles.excerpt: Hardeep Singh Puri tells CNN-News18 that oil prices 'cannot remain at their current height' for long, that India has 76–80 days of reserves, and that Western Hemisphere suppliers will step in. But he also warns of a 'totally different ball game' if the Iran war drags past March 2027.
articles.image_caption: Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The EU Just Sanctioned Iran Over Hormuz. Hours Later, the Houthis Declared a Total Ban on Israeli Shipping in the Red Sea.
articles.excerpt: Europe's first-ever freedom-of-navigation sanctions and Yemen's renewed shipping threat are closing two of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints simultaneously. India, which depends on both, has no good options.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Killed India's $23 Billion Online Gaming Industry. The Tax Bill Alone Is Unsurvivable.
articles.excerpt: Two rulings on the same day, a retrospective 28% GST on every rupee deposited, and a new law banning real-money games outright. The sector's biggest companies are already shutting down.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India, which delivered the landmark gaming verdict on May 27, 2026
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Held Rates and Fired a \$50 Billion Dollar Bazooka Instead. The Rupee Fell Anyway.
articles.excerpt: The central bank bet on NRI deposits and foreign borrowing incentives to shore up the currency. Then oil hit \$97 and wiped out the rally in a single session.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters tower in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 100,000 Fake Degrees. 28 Universities. The H-1B Fraud Bust Sending Shockwaves Through Indian America.
articles.excerpt: A former U.S. consular officer says 90 per cent of Indian H-1B applications contained fraudulent documents. Investigators have now seized the evidence to prove it.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa application data showing India as the dominant source country
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Israel Hit Iran's Petrochemical Lifeline. For India, It Means $97 Oil and No End in Sight.
articles.excerpt: The first strike on Iranian energy infrastructure since the April ceasefire sends Brent surging, the IRGC retaliating on Haifa, and the Strait of Hormuz further from reopening.
articles.image_caption: Iran's Kharg Island oil terminal, a critical export hub now targeted in the Israel-Iran conflict
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Wants Up to $2 Million Per Tanker to Cross Hormuz. India Sends a Fifth of Its Oil Through That Strait.
articles.excerpt: Tehran has drafted legislation to charge transit fees in rials, barter, or even cryptocurrency. The US has warned Oman not to cooperate. India, Japan, and every refiner in Asia is watching.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that carries a fifth of the world's oil
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
